Day 1
From Hotel: 23 min → St James Parish Church
1.St James Parish Church
A white-limestone Georgian church begun in 1774, rebuilt after the 1957 earthquake, with a Venetian chancel window unusual for a Jamaican parish church and a churchyard of 18th-century planter tombs facing Sam Sharpe Square.

39 min · 9 min → Doctor's Cave Beach
2.Doctor's Cave Beach
A private members' beach club opened in 1906 around a mineral-spring cove that made Montego Bay famous as a health resort in the 1920s; calm, clear, reef-protected water inside Montego Bay Marine Park, with loungers, a bar and changing rooms.

26 min → Rocklands Bird Sanctuary
3.Rocklands Bird Sanctuary
A hillside feeding station above Anchovy where red-billed streamertails — the doctor bird, Jamaica's national bird — and other endemic species land on an outstretched finger to drink sugar water, a tradition started by self-taught ornithologist Lisa Salmon in the 1950s.
Daily 10:00am - 5:00pm
~1 hr
Cash only, paid on arrival — around US$20 adults, no online booking or website reservation.

1.Rose Hall Great House
A restored 1770s Jamaican Georgian mansion on the hillside above the coast, Jamaica's most-visited great house and the source of the White Witch of Rose Hall legend — the reputedly murderous mistress Annie Palmer.

15 min · 2 min → Cinnamon Hill Great House
2.Cinnamon Hill Great House
A Georgian-era great house built for the Barrett family — ancestors of poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning — later bought in 1972 by Johnny Cash as a part-time home; rooms are kept much as the Cash family left them, with personal mementos throughout.

25 min → Falmouth
3.Falmouth
A meticulously planned 1769 port town, one of the Caribbean's best-preserved Georgian towns, with wide grid streets, piped water older than New York City's and rows of original merchant houses around Water Square and the old courthouse.

A one-hour, three-mile float down the Martha Brae on a hand-built thirty-foot bamboo raft poled by a licensed captain, launching from Rafter's Village on a horseshoe bend of the river named for a Taino legend of hidden Spanish gold.

Local Tastes
Jerk Chicken and Pork
Chicken and pork slow-smoked over pimento wood and coated in a scotch-bonnet marinade — Jamaica's signature street barbecue, served chopped on a board with festival · sweet fried dough · or bread.
📍 Scotchies · Pork Pit
Jamaican Patty
Flaky, turmeric-yellow curry pastry filled with spiced beef, chicken or vegetables — the island's everyday hand food, sold hot at bakeries and patty shops across Montego Bay.
📍 Juici Patties
Ackee and Saltfish
Jamaica's national dish — the buttery ackee fruit sautéed with salted cod, onion and scotch bonnet, usually eaten at breakfast with fried dumpling or festival and a side of rice and peas.
📍 Pier 1
Food Delivery
QuickCart
Foreign number: accepted. — The sign-up form's country picker lists every country, so a visiting phone number is taken at sign-up.
Jamaica's largest delivery marketplace outside Kingston, with over 200 partner restaurants across Montego Bay, Portmore and Kingston; pays in Jamaican dollars by card on delivery or online.
quickcartonline.com
7Krave
Foreign number: not required. — Sign-in uses email, Google or Facebook on the web app; no phone-number verification step was found.
A Kingston-based food-and-grocery marketplace that added Montego Bay coverage; strongest for restaurants that don't run their own delivery, with an on-demand "Hanker Order" option for anywhere not listed.
7krave.com
Getting Around
inDrive
Foreign number: accepted. — Sign-up takes any country's mobile number, verified by SMS or WhatsApp; built for exactly this cross-border case.
Uber does not operate in Montego Bay. inDrive is the app locals and visitors actually use instead — riders name their own price and nearby drivers bid on the trip, which keeps fares close to what a licensed taxi would charge without haggling in person.
indrive.com
Worth Knowing

Montego Bay splits into two very different halves, and this trip crosses both

Downtown and the Hip Strip sit west of the airport; the all-inclusive resort corridor at Rose Hall and Ironshore sits east of it. They are a real drive apart, not a stroll — budget the time this guide's motion rows show rather than assuming everything is walkable from a beachfront hotel.

Uber does not operate anywhere in Jamaica. Locals and returning visitors use inDrive, a name-your-price ride app, or a licensed JUTA taxi arranged through the hotel — don't expect the familiar app to work at the airport.

US dollars are accepted almost everywhere in the tourist zones, but change often comes back in Jamaican dollars, and small vendors, snack stands and jerk stalls are far more likely to be cash-only.

Free cancellation on the tours in this guide is worth using — Montego Bay excursions are booked well in advance in high season, but weather, especially rain on river and waterfall trips, is genuinely a same-day call.
